newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek rates jump, bonds fall on ecu/drs jitteries.
newsitem.headline: Greek rates jump, bonds fall on ecu/drs jitteries.

text.p: Greek bonds fell sharply in early trading, and depos and forex forwards jump on concerns about tighter liquidity related to forex outflows, dealers said.
All eyes were on the drachma which was losing ground against the ecu, they added.

"The drachma opened weaker against the ecu, trading around 312.30/40 on renewed ecu buying from abroad," a forex dealer at a foreign bank said. "The market is nervous and waiting to see what the Bank of Greece will do at the fixing today."

Depos and implied drachma rates from forex forwards were also taking their cues from ecu/drachma with bid rates rising half a point up to three-month tenors and five to 15 basis points from three months to one-year periods.

"Short-term bid rates are up sharply on tighter liquidity conditions due to the continued forex outflows," said a dealer at a private bank. "Longer-term rates have also risen but less than short rates."
The dealer said the market was closely watching developments in ecu/drachma to gauge the market's liquidity status.
"We might see higher rates in the next few days if forex outflows continue but I am sure that the central bank will do its best to calm the market," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank.

The higher cost of funding was also hitting fixed coupon bonds which were under selling pressure from domestic and foreign players with coupon bond prices shedding about 80 basis points, dealers said.
Some dealers said a good deal of heavy ecu buying for drachmas was due to bond sales.
"The market wants to hear more about the size of June's auctions in government bonds," said a bond dealer.
The treasury will issue 12-month T-bills at 9.60 percent on June 2, down 10 basis points, reopen bids for three-, five- and seven-year coupon bonds and auction 10-year fixed coupon bonds on June 19.
Greece auctioned three-year, 9.80 percent bonds, five-year, 9.20 percent bonds and seven-year, 8.9 percent bonds on March 19.
The finance ministry cut its three-, six- and 12-month T-bill rates by a tenth of a point to 8.50 percent, 8.80 percent and 9.60 percent respectively effective Monday, it added.
The mark was quoted at 160.23/28 from Tuesday's 160.00 fix, the dollar at 273.08/18 drachmas from 271.61 and the ecu at 312.33/43 from 311.900 drachmas.

** Two weeks at 10.50-11.00
